questions.problem:
Consider the finite region $R$ in the $xyz$-space, given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x+3y\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le z-3y\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le z\le 2}.
$$

Given the change of variables

$$
u=x+3y,\,v=z-3y,\,w=z,
$$

which of the following could be the missing part of the expression below?

$$
{∭}_{R}{cos}^{2}⁡(x+z)\operatorname{cos}⁡(z-3y)\,dV={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}\,dw\,dv\,du
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=x+3y,\,v=z-3y,\,w=z
$$

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & ={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le u\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le v\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le w\le 2}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-3-0) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{cos}^{2}⁡(x+z)\operatorname{cos}⁡(z-3y)\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}{cos}^{2}⁡(u+v)\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot |\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}{cos}^{2}⁡(u+v)\operatorname{cos}⁡v\cdot |-\frac{1}{3}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}\,\frac{1}{3}{cos}^{2}⁡(u+v)\operatorname{cos}⁡v\,\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$

$$
u=x+y,\,v=y-x,\,w=z

gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$

$$

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & ={(u,v,w)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1,\,0\le w\le 3}.\end{aligned}
$$

   

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(1+1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}

$$

 

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$ 

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2x & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(2-0) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & ={(u,v,w)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2,\,0\le w\le 1}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,\,\frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Find the volume bounded by the region $R,$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,-1\le 2y+z\le 1,\,1\le y-2z\le 4}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the volume of $R$ can be found as 

$$
V={∭}_{R}\text{d}V.
$$

Let's define a transformation $T$ as follows:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}]
$$

This transformation maps some region $Δ$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To compute the required volume, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\text{ }dV={∭}_{Δ}\text{ }f(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))\,|\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w
$$

where $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T.$

The inequalities that define the region $R,$

$$
0\le x\le 1,\,-1\le 2y+z\le 1,\,1\le y-2z\le 4,
$$

suggest that we use the change of variables

$$
u=x,\,v=2y+z,\,w=y-2z.
$$

This change of variables gives us the *inverse* function ${T}^{-1},$ that is

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}u(x,y,z) \\ v(x,y,z) \\ w(x,y,z)\end{aligned}].
$$

To compute the required volume, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $Δ,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of ${T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & ={(u,v,w)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,-1\le v\le 1,\,1\le w\le 4}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T:$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $T$ is

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}=-\frac{1}{5}.
$$

Note that $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}\ne 0$ everywhere inside $Δ.$ In other words, $T$ has no critical points inside $Δ.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}dV & ={∭}_{Δ}1\cdot |-\frac{1}{5}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{5}\,dw\,dv\,du \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}du\cdot {\int }_{-1}^{1}dv\cdot {\int }_{1}^{4}dw \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[u]_{0}^{1}\cdot [v]_{-1}^{1}\cdot [w]_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (1-0)\cdot (1-(-1))\cdot (4-1) \\  & =\frac{6}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the finite region $R$ in Cartesian $xyz$-space, given by

$$
R = \big\{ (x,y,z) \: : \:1 \leq xy \leq  2, \: 1 \leq y \leq 2, \: 0 \leq z\leq 1 \big\}.
$$

By performing the change of variables

$$
u=xy,  \qquad
v=y, \qquad
w=2z,
$$

 

write down the triple integral

$$
\displaystyle 
\iiint\limits_R 3xy^2+6yz \, \mathrm{d}V
$$

as a repeated integral in terms of $u,$ $v,$ and $w.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's define a transformation $\mathbf{T}$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096366/assets/c3c03fec53fda9106ca287f15afd0d07b1adddf00675b2bdbec8a658fbdf06aa.png)

This transformation maps some region $\Delta$ in the $uvw$-space to our region $R$ in the $xyz$-space.

To find the required integral, we can use the change of variables formula

$$
\iiint\limits_{R} f(x,y,z) \ \mathrm{d}V = \iiint\limits_{\Delta} \ f(x(u,v,w), y(u,v,w), z(u,v,w)) \: \left| \dfrac{\partial (x, y, z)}{\partial (u, v, w)} \right|  \: \textrm{d}u \textrm{d}v \textrm{d}w
$$

where $\dfrac{\partial (x, y, z)}{\partial (u, v, w)}$ is the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf{T}.$

Note that the change of variables

$$
u=xy,  \qquad
v=y, \qquad
w=2z,
$$

 

gives us the *inverse* function $\mathbf T^{-1},$ that is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096366/assets/643fb7a9bbc46ac2a6fe8c6d89f4fcb7f2db206c7af11f7cde9e1a34da8ac201.png)

To find the required integral, we proceed in four steps:

**Step 1**: Find $\Delta,$ which is the image of $R$ under the action of $\mathbf{T}^{-1}.$ 

Our domain in the $uvw$-space is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ & ={(u,v,w)\,:\,1\le u\le 2,\,1\le v\le 2,\,0\le w\le 2}.\end{aligned}
$$

  

**Step 2**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf T^{-1}{:}$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf T^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}y & x & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}y & x \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(y-0) \\  & =2y \\  & =2v.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Compute the Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf T{:}$

The Jacobian determinant corresponding to $\mathbf T$ is

$$
\dfrac{\partial (x, y, z)}{\partial (u, v, w)} = \left( \dfrac{\partial (u, v, w)}{\partial (x, y, z)} \right)^{-1} =\dfrac{1}{2v}.
$$

Note that $\dfrac{\partial (x, y, z)}{\partial (u, v, w)} \neq 0$ everywhere inside $\Delta.$ In other words, $\mathbf{T}$ has no critical points inside $\Delta.$

**Step 4**: Perform the change of variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}3x{y}^{2}+6yz\,dV & ={∭}_{Δ}(3uv+3vw)\cdot |\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}3v(u+w)\cdot |\frac{1}{2v}|\,\text{d}u\text{d}v\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{3}{2}(u+w)\,dw\,dv\,du\end{aligned}
$$
